rr1-run-the-fix.title: Verify the claimed fix by RUNNING it, not reading it
rr1-run-the-fix.imperative: Run every query primitive against the REAL shipped episodes/ directory (enumerate, enumerate --include-retired, select, neighbours, fetch). Run a create into a fresh --store-root. Record pass/fail with a finding citing actual command output.
constraints: do not edit any repo file
rr1-run-the-fix.finding: F1 symptom gone, verified by execution not reading. Against the REAL episodes/: enumerate, enumerate --include-retired, select all exit 0 (count 0); fetch/neighbours of an absent id exit 2 with 'no such episode'. Fresh --store-root: create bootstraps active/+retired/ and writes active/governor-268-001.md, exit 0. Full lifecycle in an out-of-repo store: 2 creates, retire moves the file to retired/, ordinary enumerate excludes it, --include-retired includes it, fetch by name returns status retired, C5 both directions hold.

rr2-classifier-single-rule.title: Is episode_id_for() genuinely the single membership rule?
rr2-classifier-single-rule.imperative: Audit every path that decides whether a file is an episode: all three directories, readers and writer. Does any path still make its own membership decision (a bare glob, an inline name test, a stem promotion)? Record pass/fail with a finding.
rr2-classifier-single-rule.finding: episode_id_for() IS the single rule for files the store LISTS (both layout scans + the flat-root stray scan route through it; verified by reading and by probe). It is NOT applied where an id is HANDED IN: resolve_episode_path() and is_episode_in_ordinary_search() build root/sub/f'{id}.md' from unvalidated input. Two further unnamed decisions precede the classifier in both scans: an 'if not path.is_file(): continue' silent skip, and the '*.md' glob itself (case-sensitive on POSIX, insensitive on Windows).

rr3-fifth-trap.title: Hunt a fifth trap — what does a GRAMMAR classifier get wrong that a LIST did not?
rr3-fifth-trap.imperative: Probe at minimum: well-formed-id stem with non-episode CONTENT; well-formed id in the flat root (neither active nor retired); ID_RE case sensitivity vs a case-insensitive filesystem; a .md in a nested subdirectory under active/; an astronomically long well-formed id; a file with no extension or a double extension. DEMONSTRATE anything found. Record pass/fail with a finding.
constraints: probes live outside the repo or under .agent-work/
rr3-fifth-trap.finding: FIFTH TRAP FOUND AND DEMONSTRATED: the grammar classifies NAMES THE STORE LISTS, never IDS THE STORE IS HANDED. On a demonstrably healthy store: is_episode_in_ordinary_search('../../elsewhere') -> True (silent wrong membership answer for a file outside the store); CLI 'fetch ../../elsewhere' and 'neighbours ../../elsewhere' -> 'error: half-retired store ... remove the active/ copy to complete the retirement' (a false corruption diagnosis with a DESTRUCTIVE remediation instruction, on an uncorrupted store); 'fetch old/probe-run-001' returns a record that enumerate refuses as misfiled. Also: P1 a well-formed-stem .md with non-episode content still mints a phantom id in enumerate_episode_ids; P7 a directory named <id>.md is silently skipped by is_file(); P6 a .MD file is refused on Windows and invisible on POSIX.
